title: Signed double evaluation chain map and canonical derived model
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $P,J,I$ be arbitrary cochain complexes of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume $P$ is K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] and $I,J$ are K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex], using the one-object ringed site for ordinary modules. Use the product total Hom [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], with $d(f)=d_{\mathrm{target}}f-(-1)^{|f|}fd_{\mathrm{source}}$, and direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], with $d(g\otimes x)=d_Hg\otimes x+(-1)^{|g|}g\otimes d_Px$. Write $Q$ for localization into $D(R)$, $H=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(J,I)$, $A=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,J)$, $T=\operatorname{Tot}(H\otimes_R P)$ and $B=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(A,I)$. There is a chain map $E:T\to B$ characterized, for homogeneous $g\in H^h$, $x\in P^s$, $f\in A^k$, by
$$E(g\otimes x)(f)=(-1)^{ks}g(f(x))\in I^{h+s+k}.$$
The formula is interpreted componentwise and extended linearly over the finite support in the tensor direct sum, so it requires no boundedness or finite-generation hypothesis. In component notation $g:J^{-r}\to I^p$ with $p+r=h$ and $k=-r-s$, its coefficient is $\epsilon_{p,r,s}=(-1)^{s(r+1)}$. It satisfies the differential identities $\epsilon_{p,r,s}=\epsilon_{p+1,r,s}$, $\epsilon_{p,r,s}=(-1)^s\epsilon_{p,r-1,s}$, and $\epsilon_{p,r,s+1}=(-1)^{r+1}\epsilon_{p,r,s}$.
Using derived internal Hom on the one-object ringed site [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and the K-flat tensor comparison [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model], there are canonical isomorphisms in $D(R)$
$$QT\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(QJ,QI)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QP,\qquad QB\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(QP,QJ),QI).$$
Under these isomorphisms $Q(E)$ is exactly the canonical morphism $e_{QP,QJ,QI}$ of [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-canonical-map], with its specified transpose normalization. No invertibility of $E$ or $Q(E)$ is asserted.

proof.text:
Construct the graded map using the actual Hom projections. For $h+s=n$, $g\in H^h$, $x\in P^s$ and $f\in A^k$, put
$$E_{h,s}(g,x)(f)=(-1)^{ks}g^{s+k}(f^s(x)).$$
Its value lies in $I^{n+k}$, and it is $R$-bilinear in $g,x$ and $R$-linear in $f$. The tensor-Hom universal property therefore gives $H^h\otimes_RP^s\to B^n$. Sum these maps over $h+s=n$. Each element of $T^n$ has finite support in this direct sum, so each output Hom-product coordinate is a finite sum. The infinitely many coordinates of $g$ and $f$ are accessed by projections, never summed. This gives a unique graded $R$-linear map with the required formula, for completely unbounded complexes.

source.place: Tag 0A60 (lemma-evaluate-and-more), finite-support construction preceding the sign equations

proof.text:
Check the differential on $g\otimes x$ against an arbitrary $f\in A^k$, without assuming that $g,x,f$ are cycles. The Hom differential gives
$$\begin{aligned}
(d_BE(g\otimes x))(f)
&=(-1)^{ks}d_Ig(f(x))-(-1)^{h+s+(k+1)s}g((d_Af)(x))\\
&=(-1)^{ks}d_Ig(f(x))-(-1)^{h+ks}g(d_Jf(x))
 +(-1)^{h+ks+k}g(f(d_Px)).
\end{aligned}$$
Here $d_Af=d_Jf-(-1)^kfd_P$ and $s+(k+1)s\equiv ks\pmod2$. On the other hand $d_Hg=d_Ig-(-1)^hgd_J$, so
$$E(d_Hg\otimes x)(f)+(-1)^hE(g\otimes d_Px)(f)
=(-1)^{ks}(d_Ig-(-1)^hgd_J)(f(x))+(-1)^{h+k(s+1)}g(f(d_Px)).$$
The three coefficients agree. The Hom product projections and the tensor generators determine the maps, hence $d_BE=Ed_T$. This proves that the graded construction is a chain map.

source.place: Tag 0A60 (lemma-evaluate-and-more), equations alpha and beta; explicit homogeneous verification

proof.text: For the component $g:J^{-r}\to I^p$, nonzero evaluation on $x\in P^s$ selects $k=-r-s$. Thus $ks=-rs-s^2\equiv s(r+1)\pmod2$, giving $\epsilon_{p,r,s}=(-1)^{s(r+1)}$. This is independent of $p$; replacing $r$ by $r-1$ changes the exponent by $s$, and replacing $s$ by $s+1$ changes it by $r+1$. These are precisely the three asserted differential identities, for all integer indices.

proof.text: Use the one-object site with trivial topology and ring $R$; its sheaves of modules are just $R$-modules, so all representative comparisons apply to the stated complexes. Since $I,J$ are K-injective, the definition and representative-independence of derived internal Hom give canonical isomorphisms $QH\cong R\operatorname{Hom}(QJ,QI)$ and $QA\cong R\operatorname{Hom}(QP,QJ)$. Since $I$ is K-injective, they also give $QB\cong R\operatorname{Hom}(QA,QI)$, and transport along the second isomorphism gives the asserted target. No K-injectivity of $A$ is needed: it is a source of Hom. Since $P$ is K-flat, the source tensor-model lemma computes the tensor with $H$; the native one-K-flat localization comparison permits $P$ on the right and fixes its canonical normalization. Combining it with the first Hom comparison gives the asserted source isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0A67 (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate), choices of representatives, and Section RHom preceding Tag 0A65

proof.text: Resolve only $H$: choose a K-flat quasi-isomorphism $u:U\to H$. Put $C=\operatorname{Tot}(U\otimes_RP)$ and $q=u\otimes1_P:C\to T$. The K-flat criterion makes $q$ a quasi-isomorphism, because $P$ is K-flat. Also $C$ is K-flat: for acyclic $F$, reassociate $F\otimes C$ as $(F\otimes U)\otimes P$; the first tensor is acyclic by K-flatness of $U$, and the second by that of $P$. The native complex associator gives this reassociation. We will compare maps after $Qq$, which is invertible. The native tensor comparison identifies $Qq$ with $Qu\otimes1_{QP}$; thus this reduction uses the same source isomorphism as Step 4.

source.place: Tag 0A67, replacement of representatives; K-flat tensor criterion and canonical associator

proof.text:
Write $v:A\otimes_RP\to J$ and $w:H\otimes_RJ\to I$ for ordinary evaluation, $v(f\otimes x)=f(x)$ and $w(g\otimes y)=g(y)$. These are chain maps: for either pair the Hom formula gives $d(f(x))=(df)(x)+(-1)^{|f|}f(dx)$, exactly the total-tensor differential. Define the chain map $\Psi:C\otimes_RA\to I$ by reassociating, swapping $P$ and $A$, then applying $1_U\otimes v$ and $w\circ(u\otimes1_J)$. The complex braiding formula gives
$$\Psi((z\otimes x)\otimes f)=(-1)^{ks}u(z)(f(x)),\qquad |x|=s,\ |f|=k.$$
Consequently it is exactly the ordinary uncurrying of $E\circ q:C\to\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(A,I)$, by Step 1. This equality follows on every pure tensor and every Hom projection; no commutation of tensor with infinite Hom products is used.

source.place: Tags 0A60 and 0A61 (remark-sign-explanation), swapping the last two factors before the two evaluations

proof.text: Apply the one-K-flat uncurrying normalization lemma three times. For $(U,V,I,\phi,\psi)=(C,A,I,E\circ q,\Psi)$ it says that the right-tensor derived transpose of $Q\Psi$ is $Q(E\circ q)$ under the Hom comparison, since $C$ is K-flat and $I$ K-injective. For $(A,P,J,1_A,v)$ it says that $Qv$ represents the derived evaluation $R\operatorname{Hom}(QP,QJ)\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP\to QJ$, since $P$ is K-flat and $J$ K-injective. For $(U,J,I,u,w\circ(u\otimes1_J))$ it identifies the last evaluation with the derived evaluation $R\operatorname{Hom}(QJ,QI)\otimes^{\mathbf L}QJ\to QI$ precomposed with the map $QU\to QH$, since $U$ is K-flat and $I$ K-injective. The native comparison preserves associators and braiding and is natural, so localizing the actual composite defining $\Psi$ is exactly the derived composite that swaps $QP$ past $QA$ and applies these two evaluations. All three applications allow the other tensor factor to be arbitrary.

source.place: Tags 0A61 and 0A67, normalization of the representative construction via the tensor-Hom adjunction

proof.text: The right transpose of the composite in Step 7 is the iterated evaluation of the closed-evaluation lemma. That lemma identifies its left uncurrying with $QA\otimes QH\otimes QP\to QH\otimes QJ\to QI$, swapping the first two factors, precisely the specified normalization of $e_{QP,QJ,QI}$. The signs can also be checked directly: moving a degree-$k$ element of $A$ past an output of degree $h+s$ and then applying $E$ contributes $(-1)^{k(h+s)+ks}=(-1)^{kh}$, the sign of swapping $A^k$ and $H^h$. By injectivity of the adjunction bijection, Step 7 identifies $Q(E\circ q)$ with $e$ precomposed by $Qu\otimes1$. Cancel the invertible $Qq$ and the natural source comparison from Step 5. This proves the asserted equality for $Q(E)$ under exactly the canonical isomorphisms of Step 4. Every comparison cancelled here is a representative quasi-isomorphism; $E$ itself has never been assumed invertible.
